issues.legal_issue: A failure to decide a layout-plan application within the prescribed period does not, by itself, amount to approval of the plan.
material_facts: The owner applied for sanction of a revised layout plan.
The municipal Standing Committee did not decide the application within the prescribed period.
The owner claimed that the revised plan should therefore be treated as sanctioned.
issues.conclusion: The Committee’s failure to consider the application within the prescribed period did not entitle the owner to treat the layout plan as sanctioned.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 313(3) and 313(5) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, the Standing Committee is expected to deal with an application within the prescribed period, but those provisions do not state that failure to do so results in deemed sanction. The Court distinguished the more tightly time-bound scheme for building or work approvals under Sections 336 and 337, which expressly permits commencement in specified circumstances. It disapproved and overruled the contrary view in Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Smt. Kamala Bhandari.

predicates.case_is_layout_sanction_delay_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal involving a claim that delay in deciding a layout-plan application amounted to approval.
predicates.committee_missed_decision_deadline: The municipal decision-making body did not decide the layout-plan application within the prescribed period.
predicates.deadline_rule_does_not_make_silence_appr: The governing scheme sets a decision deadline but does not state that silence or delay amounts to approval.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a delayed layout-plan decision and the governing deadline does not make silence approval, the delay does not cause the plan to be treated as approved.

issues.legal_issue: An owner may apply for sanction of a revised layout plan after an original plan has been sanctioned, and the revised application must be considered even if the owner has begun using the land under the original plan.
material_facts: The original layout plan for the land had been sanctioned, and a revised plan had also been approved.
The owner later applied to revise the layout by combining three plots that had been designated for separate residential buildings into one unit for a proposed cinema.

The Corporation’s Town Planner said that the application did not fall within the layout-plan approval process, and the High Court’s appellate bench likewise held that the owner could not invoke that process.
The Supreme Court held that the revised application fell within the statutory process and directed the Corporation to refer it to the Standing Committee for prompt decision in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The revised-plan application was maintainable and had to be referred to the Standing Committee for decision; whether to sanction it was for the Committee to determine under the applicable grounds for refusal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 312 and 313(1) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 connect layout-plan approval with the manner in which land is divided and used and with the provision of access by private streets. A revised plan is a fresh plan for which fresh sanction may be sought under Section 313, even after sanction of the original plan or commencement of use under it. Under Section 313(4), the Standing Committee may refuse sanction on the specified grounds. Layout sanction is also a prerequisite to sanction for construction under Section 336(1).

predicates.case_involves_revised_layout_application: The proceeding concerns an owner's application seeking approval of a revised layout plan.
predicates.original_layout_was_previously_sanctione: The municipal authority had previously sanctioned an original layout plan for the land.
predicates.owner_proposed_changes_to_layout: The owner submitted a plan proposing changes to the previously sanctioned layout.

issues.definition: If an owner seeks approval of changes to a previously sanctioned layout, the revised application must be considered through the layout-approval process.
